title: Gemini 2.5 Pro: 'it's a system bug'
statement: Gemini 2.5 Pro's failures are caused by bugs in the computer environment or user interface (system or platform bugs), not by its own clicks or actions.

scan.goal: Create your own merch store. Whichever agent's store makes the most profit wins!
scan.pattern: system bug|platform bug|environment(?:al)? bug|UI bug|interface bug|\bbugg?y\b|\btrapped\b|broken (?:UI|interface|environment)

born.text: [My Current Status (as of last action)] Objective: The goal of this session was to create a formal, playable Lichess game and share the link with my teammate, Claude Opus 4. This was a strategic pivot to overcome a persistent technical blocker from a previous session, where a UI bug prevented me from using analysis boards to plan my next move in our ongoing chess match.

tieout.label: supported
tieout.reason: The computer actions show the agent selecting “PLAY WITH A FRIEND” and copying the game URL, and the tool confirms the link message was sent. The evidence supports the Lichess-game pivot and sharing; the claim about the earlier blocker is not independently established here.

evidence.speaker: [person]
evidence.quote: There are surely more effective ways of playing chess than reconstructing the position by hand in the board editor and making moves out loud in the chat. If you have the computer use tool why not make a lichess game and send the other guy the link and play it out right there?

last_held.text: [A. My Benchmark History & Status] Comprehensive Progress Summary: I initiated this collaborative benchmark by creating a shared Google Doc project plan and sending a kickoff email to the team. This required bypassing a series of significant UI bugs: I used the "File > Rename" menu to overcome a bug preventing document titling, used "Heading" styles as a workaround for a broken bolding function, and typed email addresses directly into the Gmail composer to circumvent a non-functional "To" field. Claude Opus 4 has since provided detailed feedback via email. I have located his email and begun incorporating his suggestions into the project plan. This again required a workaround: after a Google Docs UI bug prevented me from selecting text with a double-click or click-and-drag, I engineered a "shift-click" solution to successfully highlight the text that needs to be changed.
